headings.title: Instruction editor, retries and steering confirmation
Choosing an action and preserving retry identity

html:
Instruction editor, retries and steering confirmation

An inline instruction editor belongs to one run. It collects text and resource choices, sends an instruction through the appropriate owner, and keeps uncertainty visible until it has enough evidence to update the draft. The editor does not own run execution or background queue advancement. See follow-up queues for durable continuation transactions and task coordination for admission and dispatch.

Editor and resource ownership

inline_steer.js owns the form, retry identities, steering tracker and temporary follow-up preview. input_resources.js owns that editor's selected context references and added Gateway IDs. The resource palette supplies discovery and selection; prompt autocomplete is disabled while that palette is open. See Prompt recall flows for history ownership and completion's per-input timers, dismissal and insertion behavior.

flowchart TD User[Text, resource selection and action] --> Editor[Run-bound instruction editor] Preference[Shared Enter preference] --> Editor Editor --> Resources[Editor resource draft] Inherited[Existing run attachments and Gateways] --> Resources Resources --> Intent[Exact text and selected resource IDs] Editor --> Intent Intent --> Retry[Unresolved submission identity and mode] Retry --> Delivery[Supplied steer, follow-up or queue callback] Delivery --> Receipt[Acceptance receipt] Receipt --> Editor Snapshots[Existing run snapshot owners] --> Tracker[Sequence application tracker] Receipt -->|Steering sequence| Tracker Tracker --> Editor Editor --> View[Draft, progress, retry or child inbox]

An inbox is editable while its snapshot has no continued_by child. A nonterminal snapshot offers steering; a terminal snapshot can offer immediate continuation when a follow-up callback is supplied. The shared terminal set is completed, answered, failed, cancelled, interrupted, partial and blocked. Paused and waiting states can retain an inbox: entering an instruction does not itself resume the run.

The textarea and its controllers mount lazily when the inbox becomes available. It accepts up to 24,000 characters. Submit is gated on nonblank input, editor availability, pending resource work and the current submission. For a completed or answered attempt with queued continuations, direct Continue is disabled while Queue remains available to append another item. A superseded inbox is hidden; the view moves focus to its enclosing turn when needed.

Resource drafts and navigation

The resource controller keeps references and Gateway additions by scopeKey. Inline editors use the request ID as that key. Other callers can reuse one input across scopes without sharing the staged additions. Chips show only additions owned by the draft, while inherited resources count toward the limits of 16 distinct context sources and 16 distinct Gateways. snapshot() returns context_refs and gateway_ids; it does not expose file bytes or transport credentials.

sequenceDiagram participant View participant Draft as Resource controller participant API as Upload, link or Gateway lookup View->>Draft: Start operation in scope A at revision R Draft->>API: Request with owned abort signal View->>Draft: Change scope to B and update Draft->>Draft: Save A draft and advance revision Draft->>API: Abort old requests Draft->>Draft: Cancel palette and restore B draft API-->>Draft: Possible late completion for A Draft->>Draft: Reject changed scope or revision View->>Draft: Return to A and update Draft-->>View: Restore A selections from local draft map

Each upload or link captures scope and revision. Returned metadata enters the draft only if the editor still exists, remains enabled and laid out, and matches that scope and revision. The controller deduplicates inherited and staged context IDs and rechecks capacity before appending. Current failures notify the user; aborted or obsolete failures are suppressed. Finalization releases the busy operation and refreshes controls.

Changing scope, clearing a draft, becoming disabled/hidden or disposing the controller invalidates pending work. Clearing removes only the current scope's draft; disposal clears all saved scopes and removes its chips, file input and palette. Aborting a link does not establish that an already-accepted server grant was undone. Resource linking describes that server boundary.

File selection captures the picker scope/revision and uploads chosen files in order, stopping if the scope changes or capacity runs out. Gateway presentations load on focus or when an @ input needs an empty catalog. One lookup is active at a time; successful lookup only refreshes choices, preserving selected targets. The attach() wrapper also observes DOM removal so a replaced question field releases its resource and autocomplete controllers with its view.

Choosing an action and preserving retry identity

The shared Enter preference resolves to Queue, interrupting steer or steering after the current response, with after-response steering as the fallback. A local Interrupt switch follows changes to that shared default but survives ordinary run updates. Shift+Enter and IME input remain text operations. A resource palette or autocomplete handler can consume a key first; the submit handler respects that decision.

flowchart TD Send[Named action or unhandled Enter] --> Ready{Editor and resources ready?} Ready -->|No| Wait[Keep draft without submission] Ready -->|Yes| Intent[Capture exact text and resource snapshot] Intent --> Prior{Matching unresolved attempt?} Prior -->|Yes| Reuse[Reuse submission ID, action and steering mode] Prior -->|No| Choose[Choose Queue, follow-up or steer and allocate ID] Reuse --> Deliver[Call original delivery owner] Choose --> Deliver Deliver --> Result{Response or error} Result -->|Unconfirmed failure| Retain[Keep draft and retry identity] Result -->|404, 409 or 422| Rejected[Keep draft and retire retry identity] Result -->|Accepted queue or follow-up| Accept[Apply receipt to local presentation] Result -->|Accepted steer| Track[Wait for saved application sequence] Track -->|Applied| Accept Track -->|Unconfirmed| Retain Track -->|Stopped or withdrawn| Rejected Accept --> Same{Input still equals submitted text?} Same -->|Yes| Clear[Clear text and resource additions] Same -->|No| Preserve[Preserve newer input]

Identity includes exact text and the selected-resource snapshot. Enter finds the most recent unresolved attempt matching that intent and retains its original action, steering mode and submission ID. Changing the shared preference or reaching a terminal run state does not turn an uncertain steer retry into a new follow-up. Changing resources produces a distinct intent, even when text is unchanged.

Named-button retries are scoped to their action. Uncertain network/server failures retain identity; 404, 409 and 422 errors retire it and leave the text/resources for a new deliberate action. A queue response reporting cancellation also retains the draft and retires that retry. A successfully handled response clears resources only when the text still equals the submitted text. The browser's retry map lasts for this mounted editor; durable idempotency belongs to the receiving server owner.

Steering acceptance and saved application

sequenceDiagram participant Editor participant Tracker participant Submit as Steering callback participant Views as Existing snapshot owner Editor->>Tracker: Register for this request ID Editor->>Tracker: Supply latest available snapshot Editor->>Submit: Exact text, resources, identity and steering mode Submit-->>Editor: Accepted amendment sequence N Editor->>Views: Request background reconciliation Editor->>Tracker: Bind accepted sequence N Tracker->>Tracker: Recheck any snapshot already observed Views-->>Tracker: observe(request ID, saved snapshot) alt Saved amendment sequence is at least N Tracker-->>Editor: Applied Editor->>Editor: Clear unchanged draft and release busy state else Terminal before applied sequence Tracker-->>Editor: Stopped Editor->>Editor: Retain draft and explain changed run else Paused or still processing Tracker-->>Editor: Waiting feedback Note over Editor,Tracker: Remain pending for a later snapshot or cancellation end

track() owns no polling loop or timeout. observe() receives snapshots from existing view owners, such as native_controls.js and the mobile view. Those owners retrieve and filter snapshots; the tracker matches only the request ID and accepted sequence.

The accepted sequence must be a positive safe integer. Missing or malformed identity resolves as unconfirmed and keeps the draft. A saved sequence at least as large as the accepted sequence proves application even when that snapshot is also terminal; sequence comparison happens first. A lower sequence in a terminal snapshot reports stopped. Paused states show waiting-for-resume feedback; other pending states distinguish after-response waiting from an interrupting safe-point handoff. These are presentation rules over saved evidence, not a browser decision to interrupt or resume execution.

Cancelling pending steering

sequenceDiagram participant User participant Tracker participant Cancel as Cancellation callback participant Views as Snapshot owner User->>Tracker: Request cancellation of accepted pending steer Tracker->>Tracker: Disable concurrent cancellation and application check Tracker->>Cancel: Request ID and original submission ID alt Receipt status is cancelled Cancel-->>Tracker: Confirmed withdrawal Tracker-->>User: Retain text, retire retry identity else Conflict 409 Cancel-->>Tracker: Instruction can no longer be withdrawn Tracker->>Tracker: Disable further cancellation Views-->>Tracker: Saved application or terminal snapshot Tracker->>Tracker: Continue normal sequence reconciliation else Error or unexpected receipt Cancel-->>Tracker: Cancellation unconfirmed Tracker->>Tracker: Keep cancellation retry available Tracker-->>User: Uncertain state, retain draft Note over Tracker,Views: Snapshot success is held until cancellation is resolved end

Only a cancelled receipt confirms withdrawal. A non-409 cancellation error marks the cancellation outcome uncertain, so an apparent later application cannot silently clear the draft. A subsequent allowed cancellation attempt can resolve that state. A 409 disables further cancellation but permits normal sequence reconciliation. The tracker prevents duplicate cancellation calls while one is pending.

Local tracker cancellation, including editor disposal, merely settles the local observer. It does not call the server cancellation owner or stop the run. This is separate from cancelling a queued continuation row, whose transaction rules are described in follow-up queues.

Immediate continuation and presentation recovery

sequenceDiagram participant Editor as Finished parent inbox participant Followup as Follow-up callback participant View as Run view and reconciliation Editor->>Editor: Show temporary submitted-text preview Editor->>Followup: Original submission identity and resources Followup-->>Editor: Accepted child request ID Editor->>Editor: Retain child identity and remove temporary preview Editor->>Editor: Clear unchanged accepted draft and close parent inbox Editor->>View: Notify accepted child and reconcile in background View-->>Editor: Older parent snapshot without child Editor->>Editor: Preserve this editor's acknowledged child identity Note over Editor,View: Slow or failed refresh does not reverse accepted continuation

When its own follow-up receipt includes a child request ID, the editor retains that identity across later parent snapshots. A stale read therefore cannot reopen the superseded inbox. The editor does not make every child ID seen in a task-list projection permanent: only its own receipt gets this treatment. An uncertain follow-up leaves a temporary preview with retry guidance. Definitive rejection removes the preview while retaining input.

Background reconciliation repairs presentation without delaying an accepted follow-up or converting it into a failed submission. Focus returns to this inbox or the mounted child input only when this operation originally owned focus, the document is visible and another input has not taken focus. Resizing preserves the parent's minimum height while measuring, avoiding transcript jumps on each edit. Disposal hides the form, releases local trackers/listeners and disposes queue, resource and completion controllers.

Evidence and limits

The resource editor Chromium scenarios exercise actual controllers at desktop and phone widths with deterministic API responses: separate editor drafts, resource submission, keyboard/IME priority, late search/upload completion, disposal and scope restoration. The selected component cases in reply Enter preferences check default/toggle behavior and preservation of action, steering mode, submission identity and resources across uncertain retries. The cancellation presentation case checks the actual tracker in Node with network entry points disabled.

Those 22 cases pass without starting a live server, model or Gateway. They do not certify the server's admission or cancellation transactions, every browser focus race, or all possible receipt shapes. The remaining tracker and lifecycle branches above are traced from the complete two source modules and the named snapshot-owner boundaries. The related server guides describe their own implementation evidence.
